questions.text: Which choice is a complete sentence?
options: Because the research team finished the experiment early.
The research team finished the experiment early.
Finishing the experiment early after several delays.
While the research team was working late in the lab.
questions.explanation: A complete sentence needs a subject, a finite verb, and a complete thought.

questions.text: Which choice is a sentence fragment?
options: The museum closes at six on weekdays.
Visitors waited outside until the doors opened.
Although the museum closes at six on weekdays.
The final tour begins at five thirty.
questions.explanation: “Although” makes the clause dependent; it cannot stand alone.

questions.text: Which choice is a complete sentence?
options: The students preparing for the competition in the library.
The students prepared for the competition in the library.
Preparing for the competition in the library.
questions.explanation: “Prepared” is a finite past-tense verb and completes the sentence.

questions.text: In the sentence “Running every morning improves Maya’s concentration,” what is the role of the word “Running”?
options: A gerund functioning as a noun
A past participle functioning as an adjective
A finite verb showing past tense
questions.explanation: “Running” names an activity and serves as the subject, so it is a gerund.

questions.text: Which choice contains a past participle used as part of a verb phrase?
options: The students write summaries every Friday.
The students have written three summaries this week.
The students are writing summaries now.
questions.explanation: “Written” is the third form/past participle used with the auxiliary “have.”

questions.text: Which choice correctly completes the sentence? “Last year, the school ___ a new science lab, and since then it has ___ several research projects.”
questions.explanation: The first blank needs V2 past tense “opened”; the second uses V3 “supported” after “has.”

questions.text: Which choice is a complete sentence?
options: The painting displayed near the entrance.
Displayed near the entrance, the painting attracted a crowd.
The painting, displayed near the entrance.
Having been displayed near the entrance.
questions.explanation: The main clause “the painting attracted a crowd” is complete; the opening participial phrase only modifies it.

questions.text: Which choice is a fragment?
options: The athletes who trained every morning improved steadily.
The athletes trained every morning and improved steadily.
The athletes who trained every morning.
Because the athletes trained every morning, they improved steadily.
questions.explanation: The relative clause “who trained every morning” does not provide a main finite verb for the full sentence.

questions.text: Which revision turns the fragment into a complete sentence? “After reviewing the final data from the experiment.”
options: After reviewing the final data from the experiment carefully.
After reviewing the final data from the experiment in the lab.
After reviewing the final data from the experiment, the researchers revised their conclusion.
After the final data from the experiment.
questions.explanation: Choice C adds an independent clause with subject “researchers” and finite verb “revised.”

questions.text: In which sentence is the -ing form functioning as a gerund rather than as part of a verb phrase?
options: The class is studying linear functions.
Studying linear functions requires careful attention to slope.
The class was studying when the bell rang.
The students are studying after school.
questions.explanation: “Studying linear functions” functions as the subject of the sentence, so “Studying” is a gerund.

questions.text: Which choice is a complete sentence despite the long modifier?
options: The new telescope, designed by engineers from three universities and tested for nearly two years.
The new telescope, designed by engineers from three universities, captured its first image last night.
Designed by engineers from three universities and tested for nearly two years.
The new telescope designed by engineers from three universities.
questions.explanation: The main clause is “The new telescope captured its first image last night.”

questions.text: Which statement best explains why “The results published in the journal last month” is a fragment?
options: “Published” is a third-form participle modifying “results,” so the phrase lacks a finite main verb.
“Published” is a past-tense verb, but the sentence lacks a subject.
The phrase is complete because every sentence can end after a participle.
questions.explanation: Without an auxiliary such as “were,” “published” acts as a participle modifying “results,” not as the main finite verb.

questions.text: Which choice correctly uses the second and third forms of the verb “write”?
options: She has wrote the report after she written the outline.
She wrote the report after she had written the outline.
She written the report after she had wrote the outline.
She has written the report after she had wrote the outline.
questions.explanation: V2 is “wrote”; V3 is “written,” which follows “had.”

questions.text: Which choice is a fragment?
options: The committee, after reviewing the proposal and interviewing the candidates, announced its decision.
After the committee reviewed the proposal, it interviewed the candidates.
The committee reviewing the proposal and interviewing the candidates before the deadline.
The committee reviewed the proposal before it interviewed the candidates.
questions.explanation: “Reviewing” and “interviewing” are participles; there is no finite main verb.

questions.text: Which revision most clearly creates a complete sentence while preserving the original meaning? “The students selected for the final round because of their strong preliminary scores.”
options: The students selected for the final round because of their strong preliminary scores.
Because of their strong preliminary scores, the students selected for the final round.
The students were selected for the final round because of their strong preliminary scores.
Selected for the final round because of their strong preliminary scores.
questions.explanation: Adding the auxiliary “were” turns “selected” into the finite verb phrase “were selected.”

questions.text: Which choice correctly joins the two complete sentences? “The forecast predicted heavy rain ___ the game continued as scheduled.”
questions.explanation: A semicolon can join two closely related independent clauses.

questions.text: Which choice correctly completes the sentence? “The forecast predicted heavy rain, ___ the game continued as scheduled.”
questions.explanation: “But” creates a logical contrast and correctly follows a comma between two independent clauses.

questions.text: Which transition best shows a result? “The roads were covered in ice. ___, the school delayed its opening.”
questions.explanation: The delayed opening is a result of the icy roads.

questions.text: Which transition best shows contrast? “The first experiment produced clear results. ___, the second experiment was inconclusive.”
questions.explanation: The second result contrasts with the first.

questions.text: Which choice correctly separates the sentences? “The lecture ended early ___ several students stayed to ask questions.”
questions.explanation: Both sides are independent clauses, so a semicolon works.

questions.text: Which choice correctly completes the sentence? “The researcher reached one clear conclusion ___ the new treatment reduced recovery time.”
questions.explanation: The first clause is complete, and the second clause explains the “one clear conclusion,” so a colon is appropriate.

questions.text: Which choice is punctuated correctly?
options: The data were incomplete, therefore the team repeated the trial.
The data were incomplete; therefore, the team repeated the trial.
The data were incomplete therefore; the team repeated the trial.
The data were incomplete: therefore the team repeated the trial.
questions.explanation: A conjunctive adverb between two independent clauses is commonly preceded by a semicolon and followed by a comma.

questions.text: Which transition best completes the text? “The library extended its weekend hours to serve more students. ___, it added a quiet study room for group projects.”
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds another service in the same direction.

questions.text: Which choice correctly completes the sentence? “The team wanted to publish immediately ___ the lead researcher insisted on checking the calculations again.”
questions.explanation: The clauses contrast, and comma + “but” correctly joins them.

questions.text: Which choice avoids a comma splice?
options: The exhibit was popular, it remained open for another month.
The exhibit was popular; it remained open for another month.
The exhibit was popular, however it remained open for another month.
The exhibit was popular, remaining open, for another month.
questions.explanation: A semicolon correctly separates the two independent clauses.

questions.text: Which choice best completes the text? “The software was designed to make scheduling easier. It reduced the time needed to assign shifts by half. ___, several employees reported that the new interface was confusing.”
questions.explanation: The final sentence introduces a drawback despite the benefit, so a contrast transition is needed.

questions.text: Which choice correctly completes the sentence? “The committee considered three options ___ postpone the launch, reduce the project’s scope, or request additional funding.”
questions.explanation: The clause before the blank is complete and introduces a list, so a colon is correct.

questions.text: Which choice is punctuated correctly?
options: The sample size was small; nevertheless, the pattern was consistent across all three trials.
The sample size was small, nevertheless; the pattern was consistent across all three trials.
The sample size was small: nevertheless, the pattern was consistent across all three trials.
The sample size was small nevertheless, the pattern was consistent across all three trials.
questions.explanation: “Nevertheless” links two independent clauses and should be preceded by a semicolon and followed by a comma.

questions.text: Which transition best completes the text? “Most desert plants conserve water by limiting moisture loss through their leaves. The creosote bush, ___, can survive long dry periods by dropping some leaves entirely.”
questions.explanation: The creosote bush illustrates the general statement with a specific example.

questions.text: Which choice correctly completes the sentence? “The first survey suggested that students preferred online homework ___ the follow-up survey, conducted after a month of classroom use, showed a slight preference for paper assignments.”
questions.explanation: Two complete clauses contrast; semicolon + “however,” correctly expresses and punctuates that relationship.

questions.text: What is the slope of the line through the points (1, 3) and (5, 11)?
What is the y-intercept of y = 4x − 7?
questions.explanation: In y = mx + b, the y-intercept is b = −7.

questions.text: What is the x-intercept of y = 3x − 12?
Which equation has slope 5 and y-intercept −2?
questions.explanation: Slope-intercept form is y = mx + b.

questions.text: A line is parallel to y = −3x + 8. What is the slope of the parallel line?
questions.explanation: Parallel lines have equal slopes.

questions.text: A line is perpendicular to y = 2x + 1. What is its slope?
questions.explanation: Perpendicular slopes are negative reciprocals, so 2 becomes −1/2.

questions.text: Which equation represents the line with slope −2 passing through (3, 5)?
questions.explanation: Using y−5 = −2(x−3) gives y = −2x + 11.

questions.text: What is the solution to the system y = 2x + 1 and y = −x + 7?
questions.explanation: Set 2x+1 = −x+7, so 3x=6, x=2 and y=5.

questions.text: A gym charges a one-time registration fee of $25 plus $18 per month. In the linear model C = 18m + 25, what does 18 represent?
questions.explanation: The slope is the rate of change: $18 per month.

questions.text: The graph of f(x) = 3x − 4 is translated up 6 units. Which equation represents the new graph?
questions.explanation: A vertical shift up 6 adds 6 to the output: 3x−4+6 = 3x+2.

questions.text: Which equation represents the line through (−2, 5) and (4, −7)?
A school sold 120 tickets to a play. Student tickets cost $6 and adult tickets cost $10. Total revenue was $920. How many adult tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Let a be adults and s students. a+s=120 and 10a+6s=920. Substitution gives 4a=200, so a=50.

questions.text: The line y = kx + 4 is perpendicular to the line 3x − 2y = 8. What is k?
questions.explanation: 3x−2y=8 becomes y=(3/2)x−4, so the perpendicular slope is −2/3.

questions.text: The line y = 4x − 9 is translated up p units and then intersects the y-axis at 6. What is p?
questions.explanation: After shifting up p, the y-intercept is −9+p. Set −9+p=6 to get p=15.

questions.text: A line has x-intercept 6 and y-intercept −3. Which equation represents the line?

Ecologist Mara Chen studies desert plants. Her latest paper focuses on the saguaro cactus, _____ can survive for more than a century under favorable conditions.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The clause adds extra information about a specific noun, “the saguaro cactus,” so “which” begins a nonessential clause already preceded by a comma; the closing comma comes later in the sentence.

questions.text:
The students _____ completed the optional laboratory assignment received additional feedback from the instructor.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The clause identifies which students received feedback, so it is essential and should not be set off with commas.

questions.text:
Dr. Naila Karim, _____, will lead the field expedition next month.
Which choice best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The phrase renames the already identified person and is nonessential. A comma appears before the blank, and the comma after the blank closes the appositive.

questions.text:
The bicycle that has the red frame _____ to my brother.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: “That has the red frame” identifies which bicycle, so no commas separate the clause from the sentence.

questions.text:
The telescope, which was installed in 2024, _____ images of distant galaxies every night.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: After the nonessential clause is removed, the main sentence is “The telescope collects images…,” so the singular finite verb “collects” is required.

questions.text:
Historian Leila Morgan’s first book _____ examined trade routes across Central Asia, won a national award.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The clause gives extra information about a specific book and must be enclosed by commas on both sides.

questions.text:
The researchers analyzed samples from glaciers _____ have remained frozen for thousands of years.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The clause specifies which glaciers supplied the samples, so it is essential and takes no commas.

questions.text:
Amina’s older brother Arman _____ works as an aerospace engineer _____ helped her build the model rocket.
Which choice correctly punctuates the nonessential information?
questions.explanation: Commas, paired dashes, or parentheses can all correctly set off a truly nonessential interruption, provided the pair is used consistently.

questions.text:
The conference’s keynote speaker, Professor Elena Ruiz _____ presented new evidence about early migration patterns.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: “Professor Elena Ruiz” is an appositive identifying the keynote speaker. Because the phrase begins after a comma, a second comma must close it.

questions.text:
The books _____ are stored in the locked cabinet may be consulted only with a librarian present.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The clause identifies which books have the restriction, so it is essential. “That” without commas is the clearest SAT-style construction.

questions.text:
A conservation team is tracking one particular snow leopard. The animal _____ was fitted with a satellite collar in May _____ has traveled more than 300 kilometers since then.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The passage has already identified one specific animal. The information about the collar is therefore extra, so it should be enclosed by commas.

questions.text:
The laboratory’s two microscopes are used for different purposes. The microscope _____ has the higher magnification is reserved for cellular imaging.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Because there are two microscopes, the clause must identify which one is meant. It is essential and should not be set off by commas.

questions.text:
The novel’s narrator, a retired physician who has returned to his hometown after thirty years _____ gradually reveals why he left.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The appositive beginning after “narrator” must be closed before the main verb “reveals.” A comma correctly closes that nonessential information.

questions.text:
The archaeological site—located beneath a modern market _____ contains remains from three historical periods.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: A nonessential phrase opened with a dash must be closed with a matching dash before the main clause continues.

questions.text:
Only participants _____ completed both stages of the experiment were included in the final analysis; the other participants’ data were excluded.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: “Only participants who completed…” restricts the group. The clause is essential to meaning and therefore takes no commas.

questions.text:
The expedition required three basic supplies _____ water, navigation equipment, and first-aid kits.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The words before the blank form a complete sentence, and the list explains what the three supplies are, so a colon is correct.

questions.text:
The experiment produced one unexpected result _____ the control group improved more than the treatment group.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The first clause is complete, and the second part explains the “unexpected result.”

questions.text:
The observatory _____ built on a remote mountain in 1998 _____ has recorded thousands of stellar events.
Which choice correctly punctuates the nonessential information?
questions.explanation: The inserted phrase is nonessential, and all three paired punctuation methods can correctly set it off.

questions.text:
The museum acquired artifacts from three locations: Almaty, Kazakhstan; Tbilisi, Georgia; _____ Baku, Azerbaijan.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Because each list item already contains a comma, semicolons separate the items clearly; the final item is introduced by “; and.”

questions.text: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
options: The team needed: more time to complete the survey.
The team needed one thing: more time to complete the survey.
The team: needed more time to complete the survey.
The team needed more: time to complete the survey.
questions.explanation: A colon must follow a complete clause. “The team needed one thing” is complete and the phrase after the colon explains that thing.

questions.text:
The field team packed several specialized tools _____ a soil corer, used to collect deep samples; a spectrometer, used to identify minerals; and a drone, used to map the site.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The complete clause introduces a list. Because the list items themselves contain commas, semicolons correctly separate the items after the colon.

questions.text:
The proposed bridge _____ if approved by the city council _____ would connect the two neighborhoods.
Which choice correctly punctuates the nonessential clause?
questions.explanation: The conditional interruption is removable from the core sentence, so commas, dashes, or parentheses may all set it off when paired consistently.

questions.text:
The researchers reached a clear conclusion _____ the decline was caused by several factors rather than a single event.
Which punctuation mark most logically completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: The words “The researchers reached a clear conclusion” form a complete clause, and the following clause states the conclusion itself, so a colon is appropriate.

questions.text:
The committee interviewed candidates from Astana, Kazakhstan _____ Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan _____ and Tashkent, Uzbekistan.
Which pair of punctuation marks best completes the sentence?
questions.explanation: Each list item includes an internal comma between city and country, so semicolons are needed between the larger items.

questions.text: Which sentence correctly uses paired dashes?
options: The sculpture—created from recycled metal, was installed downtown.
The sculpture created—from recycled metal—was installed downtown.
The sculpture—created from recycled metal—was installed downtown.
The sculpture—created from recycled metal was installed—downtown.
questions.explanation: The removable phrase “created from recycled metal” is correctly enclosed by two dashes.

questions.text:
The survey measured three variables _____ students’ weekly study time, reported in hours; their average nightly sleep, reported in hours; and their self-rated stress, reported on a ten-point scale.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The complete clause “The survey measured three variables” introduces a list. The internal semicolons correctly separate complex items.

questions.text:
The biologist’s conclusion was surprising _____ namely, the species, once thought to be strictly nocturnal, was also active shortly after sunrise.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The first clause is complete and the remainder explains the surprising conclusion. A colon can introduce “namely” plus the explanation.

questions.text:
The archive contains letters from three scientists _____ Marie Curie, who studied radioactivity; Jagadish Chandra Bose, who investigated plant responses; and Chien-Shiung Wu, who conducted groundbreaking work in nuclear physics.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The first clause is complete and introduces a list. Semicolons inside the list separate entries that already contain commas.

questions.text:
The new policy—according to the committee’s final report _____ will take effect in January.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The nonessential interruption begins with a dash and must end with a matching dash.

questions.text: Which sentence is punctuated most effectively?
options: The laboratory uses three imaging methods, magnetic resonance imaging, which maps soft tissue; computed tomography, which produces cross-sectional images; and ultrasound, which uses sound waves.
The laboratory uses three imaging methods: magnetic resonance imaging, which maps soft tissue; computed tomography, which produces cross-sectional images; and ultrasound, which uses sound waves.
The laboratory uses three imaging methods; magnetic resonance imaging, which maps soft tissue, computed tomography, which produces cross-sectional images, and ultrasound, which uses sound waves.
The laboratory uses three imaging methods: magnetic resonance imaging which maps soft tissue, computed tomography which produces cross-sectional images, and ultrasound which uses sound waves.
questions.skill: Colon and semicolons in complex list
questions.explanation: The complete opening clause introduces the list with a colon, and semicolons separate list items that contain internal commas.

questions.text:
What is the solution to the system?
x + y = 10
x - y = 2
questions.explanation: Adding the equations gives 2x = 12, so x = 6; then y = 4.

questions.text: The lines y = 3x + 2 and y = 3x - 5 have how many points of intersection?
questions.explanation: The lines have the same slope but different y-intercepts, so they are parallel and never intersect.

questions.text: Which inequality represents the statement “x is at least 12”?
questions.explanation: “At least” means greater than or equal to.

questions.text: Which point satisfies y > 2x + 1?
questions.explanation: For (1,4), 4 > 2(1)+1 = 3, so the inequality is true.

questions.text: Which system has infinitely many solutions?
questions.explanation: The second equation simplifies to y = 2x + 3, so both equations describe the same line.

questions.text: A school sold 120 tickets to a performance. Student tickets cost $5 and adult tickets cost $8. The total revenue was $780. How many adult tickets were sold?
questions.explanation: Let s+a=120 and 5s+8a=780. Substituting s=120-a gives 600+3a=780, so a=60.

questions.text:
For what value of k does the system have no solution?
y = 4x + 7
2y = kx - 6
questions.explanation: The second equation is y=(k/2)x-3. For no solution, its slope must be 4, so k/2=4 and k=8; the intercepts are different.

questions.text:
Which ordered pair satisfies both inequalities?
y ≥ x - 1
y < -x + 5
questions.explanation: For (1,1): 1≥0 and 1<4. The other choices fail at least one inequality.

questions.text:
Solve the system:
3x + y = 17
x - y = 3
What is the value of x?
questions.explanation: Adding the equations gives 4x=20, so x=5.

questions.text: A concert venue can hold at most 900 people. If x is the number of students and y is the number of adults, which inequality represents the capacity constraint?
questions.explanation: “At most 900” means the total cannot exceed 900, so x+y≤900.

questions.text:
For what value of c does the system have infinitely many solutions?
6x - 4y = 10
3x - 2y = c
questions.explanation: Dividing the first equation by 2 gives 3x-2y=5. Thus c=5.

questions.text: A student has $72 to spend on notebooks and pens. Each notebook costs $6 and each pen costs $3. The student must buy at least 4 notebooks and at least 6 pens. Which system models the situation, where n is notebooks and p is pens?
questions.explanation: The budget is a maximum, so cost≤72; “at least” gives n≥4 and p≥6.

questions.text:
The system
2x + 3y = 7
4x + 6y = k
has no solution when which condition is true?
questions.explanation: Doubling the first equation gives 4x+6y=14. If k=14, the lines are identical; any other k gives parallel distinct lines and no solution.

questions.text: A point (a,b) lies in the solution region of the system y > 2x - 4 and y ≤ -x + 8. Which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: Substituting x=a and y=b directly yields b>2a-4 and b≤-a+8, which is equivalent to 2a-4<b≤-a+8.

questions.text:
A system is given by
y = 5x - 9
y = -2x + 26
What is the x-coordinate of the solution?
questions.explanation: Set the equations equal: 5x-9=-2x+26, so 7x=35 and x=5.

questions.text:
After reviewing the data _____ the researchers repeated the experiment.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The introductory phrase “After reviewing the data” should be followed by a comma before the independent clause.

questions.text:
Walking through the gallery, _____.
Which choice completes the sentence without creating a dangling modifier?
options: Maya noticed several unusually bright paintings
there were several unusually bright paintings
the brightness of the paintings was obvious
questions.explanation: The person walking through the gallery must be the subject immediately following the introductory modifier; Maya is the logical subject.

questions.text:
The first trial failed _____ the second trial produced clear results.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Both sides are independent clauses, so a semicolon can join them. A comma alone would create a comma splice.

questions.text:
Covered in fresh snow, _____ was difficult to see from the road.
Which choice completes the sentence logically?
options: the hikers saw the mountain peak
questions.explanation: The thing covered in snow is the mountain peak, so it must immediately follow the modifying phrase.

questions.text:
The laboratory had one rule _____ all samples had to be labeled before storage.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The first part is a complete sentence, and the second part explains the one rule, so a colon is appropriate.

questions.text:
The telescope, positioned on a remote plateau, _____ images with very little atmospheric distortion.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Removing the nonessential phrase leaves “The telescope captures images…,” so the singular finite verb is required.

questions.text:
The deadline _____ however _____ was extended by two weeks.
Which pair of punctuation marks best completes the sentence?
questions.skill: Transition in the middle of a sentence
questions.explanation: When “however” interrupts one independent clause, it is nonessential and is enclosed by commas.

questions.text:
Based on the latest satellite images, _____.
Which choice completes the sentence without a dangling modifier?
options: the storm appeared to be moving east
meteorologists concluded that the storm was moving east
there was evidence that the storm was moving east
the eastward movement of the storm was clear
questions.explanation: The people using the images are the meteorologists, so they must be the subject immediately after the introductory modifier.

questions.text:
The team practiced for months _____ nevertheless, it lost the opening match.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: Two independent clauses connected by a strong transition require a period or semicolon before the transition; “; nevertheless,” is correct.

questions.text: Researchers found a shell in the cave that was 40,000 years old. Which revision most clearly places the modifier?
options: Researchers found a shell in the cave that was 40,000 years old.
Researchers found in the 40,000-year-old cave a shell.
In the cave, researchers found a 40,000-year-old shell.
Researchers, 40,000 years old, found a shell in the cave.
questions.explanation: Placing “40,000-year-old” directly before “shell” makes it unambiguous that the shell, not the cave, has that age.

questions.text:
Hoping to reduce the amount of time required to process the data, _____.
Which choice completes the sentence most logically?
options: a new algorithm was developed by the team
the team developed a new algorithm
processing time was reduced by a new algorithm
there was a new algorithm developed by the team
questions.explanation: The team is the one hoping to reduce processing time, so “the team” must immediately follow the introductory modifier.

questions.text:
The measurements were unusually consistent _____ therefore, the researchers repeated the procedure with a larger sample.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: “Therefore” links two independent clauses. A semicolon before the transition and comma after it is correct.

questions.text: The report described fossils discovered near the river that were unusually well preserved. Which revision best eliminates the misplaced modifier?
options: The report described fossils that were unusually well preserved discovered near the river.
The report described unusually well-preserved fossils discovered near the river.
Discovered near the river, the report described unusually well-preserved fossils.
The report, discovered near the river, described unusually well-preserved fossils.
questions.explanation: The adjective phrase is placed directly before “fossils,” making the intended meaning clear without creating a dangling modifier.

questions.text:
The committee considered three proposals _____ one focused on public transit; another addressed pedestrian safety; and the third expanded protected bicycle lanes.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The first clause is complete and introduces three items. A colon is appropriate, and semicolons separate the complex items.

questions.text:
After examining the samples under two different microscopes _____ and comparing the images with earlier measurements, the researchers revised their conclusion.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The introductory modifying phrase continues through “and comparing…,” so no punctuation should split the parallel -ing phrases before the main clause.

questions.text:
The collection of ancient maps _____ stored in a climate-controlled room.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject is singular “collection,” not the nearby plural noun “maps,” so the singular verb “is” is required.

questions.text:
The two _____ notebooks were left on the laboratory table.
Which choice correctly shows that the notebooks belong to two scientists?
questions.explanation: For a plural noun already ending in -s, possession is shown by adding only an apostrophe: scientists’.

questions.text:
The robot adjusted _____ position before beginning the second trial.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: “Its” is the possessive pronoun. “It’s” is a contraction meaning “it is” or “it has.”

questions.text:
_____ planning to submit the final report tomorrow.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: “They’re” means “they are,” which correctly completes the sentence.

questions.text:
I wonder why the birds migrate thousands of kilometers every year_____
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The entire sentence is a statement beginning “I wonder,” not a direct question, so it ends with a period.

questions.text:
A series of experiments conducted over several months _____ that the material becomes weaker at high temperatures.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The subject “A series” is singular; the plural noun “experiments” is inside a prepositional phrase and does not control the verb.

questions.text:
The _____ migration routes were mapped using satellite data collected over ten years.
Which choice correctly shows that the routes belong to multiple birds?
questions.explanation: The plural noun “birds” ends in -s, so plural possession is “birds’.”

questions.text:
The research team revised _____ hypothesis after reviewing the new evidence.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: “Their” is the possessive determiner used before the noun “hypothesis.”

questions.text:
The architect _____ designs are displayed in the museum will speak at the conference.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: “Whose” is possessive and means “the architect’s designs.” “Who’s” means “who is” or “who has.”

questions.text:
_____ the researchers identify a statistically significant pattern?
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: A direct question begins with the helping verb before the subject: “Did the researchers identify…?”

questions.text:
Neither the lead researcher nor the laboratory assistants _____ willing to release the preliminary data before the review was complete.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: With neither/nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject. “Assistants” is plural, so “were” is required.

questions.text:
Each of the three satellite images _____ a slightly different pattern of cloud formation.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: “Each” is singular, so it takes the singular verb “shows.”

questions.text:
The company updated _____ safety procedures after an independent review found several weaknesses.
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The procedures belong to the company, so the possessive “its” is required.

questions.text:
The scientists asked whether the newly observed signal had originated outside the galaxy_____
Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: The sentence reports what the scientists asked; it is not itself a direct question, so it ends with a period.

questions.text:
The children's museum updated _____ exhibits after several teachers reported that _____ descriptions were difficult for younger visitors to understand.
Which pair of choices completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.explanation: “Its exhibits” shows possession by the singular museum. “Their descriptions” refers to the plural exhibits.

questions.text: A bag contains red and blue marbles in a ratio of 4:6. If there are 50 marbles total, how many are red?
questions.explanation: There are 10 total ratio parts. Each part is 5 marbles, so red marbles = 4×5 = 20.

questions.text: A printer produces 8 pages in 2 minutes at a constant rate. How many pages does it produce in 10 minutes?
questions.explanation: The printer produces 4 pages per minute, so in 10 minutes it produces 40 pages.

questions.text: What is 35% of 200?
If 3 notebooks cost $12 at a constant unit price, how much do 5 notebooks cost?
questions.explanation: The unit price is $4 per notebook, so 5 cost $20.

questions.text: A car travels 240 kilometers in 4 hours at a constant speed. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = distance/time = 240/4 = 60 km/h.

questions.text: The ratio of girls to boys in a club is 4:3. If there are 35 students in the club, how many are boys?
questions.explanation: There are 7 ratio parts; each part is 5 students. Boys = 3×5 = 15.

questions.text: A jacket originally costs $80 and is discounted by 25%. What is the sale price?
questions.explanation: A 25% discount is $20, so the sale price is $80−$20=$60.

questions.text: A recipe uses flour and sugar in the ratio 5:2. If 350 grams of flour are used, how many grams of sugar are needed?
questions.explanation: 350 corresponds to 5 parts, so one part is 70 grams and sugar is 2×70=140 grams.

questions.text: A cyclist travels 18 miles in 1.5 hours at a constant rate. What is the cyclist’s speed in miles per hour?
questions.explanation: 18÷1.5=12 miles per hour.

questions.text: A school’s enrollment increased from 800 students to 920 students. What was the percent increase?
questions.explanation: The increase is 120. Divide by the original 800: 120/800=0.15=15%.

questions.text: After a 20% increase, the price of a device is $360. What was the original price?
questions.explanation: If the original price is x, then 1.20x=360, so x=300.

questions.text: A solution contains water and concentrate in the ratio 7:3. After 20 liters of water are added, the ratio becomes 3:1. How many liters of concentrate were in the original solution?
questions.explanation: Let original amounts be 7k water and 3k concentrate. Then (7k+20)/(3k)=3, so 7k+20=9k, k=10, and concentrate=3k=30 liters.

questions.text: A car travels 90 kilometers in 1.5 hours. At the same rate, how many meters will it travel in 40 seconds?
questions.explanation: 90 km/1.5 h = 60 km/h = 60,000 m/3,600 s = 50/3 m/s. In 40 s it travels about 666.7 m.

questions.text: A quantity is increased by 25% and then decreased by 20%. The final value is what percent of the original value?
questions.explanation: Multiply by 1.25 and then by 0.80: 1.25×0.80=1.00, so the final value is 100% of the original.

questions.text: In a survey, the ratio of students who prefer option A to those who prefer option B is 5:7. If 18 more students prefer B than A, how many students prefer B?
questions.explanation: The difference is 2 ratio parts and equals 18, so one part is 9. B has 7 parts, so 7×9=63.

questions.text: Every winter, the research station _____ average snowfall at the same five locations.
questions.explanation: “Every winter” signals a repeated action, so “measures” is the correct simple present form.

questions.text: In 2022, engineers _____ the bridge after inspectors found cracks in two support beams.
questions.explanation: The completed action occurred in 2022, so “repaired” is required.

questions.text: Since the museum opened, it _____ more than three million visitors.
questions.explanation: “Since the museum opened” connects a past starting point to the present: “has welcomed.”

questions.text: By the time the rescue team arrived, the hikers _____ a temporary shelter.
questions.explanation: The shelter was completed before the rescue team arrived, so “had built” marks the earlier past action.

questions.text: By next May, the laboratory _____ all 600 samples in the collection.
questions.explanation: “By next May” calls for an action completed before a future deadline: “will have analyzed.”

questions.text: This semester, Professor Malik _____ at a second campus while a colleague is on leave.
questions.explanation: “This semester” describes a temporary current arrangement, so “is teaching” fits best.

questions.text: The astronomers _____ the telescope when a sudden power failure interrupted the observation.
questions.explanation: The calibration was in progress when the power failure interrupted it: “were calibrating.”

questions.text: The researchers _____ the same coral reef for five years, and the project is still continuing.
questions.explanation: The action began five years ago and is still continuing, so “have been monitoring” is correct.

questions.text: When the bus finally arrived, the passengers _____ in the rain for nearly an hour.
questions.explanation: The waiting continued for nearly an hour before the bus arrived: “had been waiting.”

questions.text: At 8:00 tomorrow evening, the team _____ data from the final field site.
questions.explanation: At a specific time tomorrow, the action will be in progress: “will be collecting.”

questions.text: By June, Dr. Chen _____ at the observatory for exactly ten years.
questions.explanation: “By June” plus “for exactly ten years” emphasizes duration up to a future point: “will have been working.”

questions.text: When historians reexamined the letters in 2025, they discovered that an earlier archivist _____ several dates incorrectly.
questions.explanation: The incorrect recording happened before historians reexamined the letters, so “had recorded” is correct.

questions.text: The city _____ air-quality data continuously since the sensor network was installed in 2018.
questions.explanation: “Since ... 2018” requires a present-perfect form; among the choices, “has collected” is correct.

questions.text: The archive contains thousands of photographs _____ daily life in the city during the 1930s.
questions.explanation: “Documenting” is a participle modifying “photographs”; no additional finite verb is needed.

questions.text: For more than a decade, the university _____ the historic theater building next to its main library.
questions.explanation: “Own” is normally stative, so the correct perfect form is “has owned,” not a progressive form.

questions.text: The new telescope can detect fainter objects than its predecessor. _____, it can collect images at a much faster rate.
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds another advantage of the telescope, so “Moreover” fits.

questions.text: The team expected the coating to reduce heat loss. _____, the treated surface performed no better than the untreated one.
questions.explanation: The actual result contradicts the team’s expectation, so “However” is correct.

questions.text: A landslide blocked the only road into the valley. _____, deliveries were delayed for three days.
questions.explanation: The blocked road caused the delivery delay, so “Consequently” expresses the result.

questions.text: Some desert animals avoid daytime heat by becoming active after sunset. _____, kangaroo rats often forage at night.
questions.explanation: Kangaroo rats provide a specific example of desert animals being active at night.

questions.text: The researchers first removed duplicate records from the database. _____, they standardized the spelling of location names.
questions.explanation: After duplicate records were removed, the next step was standardizing location names.

questions.text: The policy does not ban private vehicles from downtown. _____, it limits the hours during which they may enter certain streets.
questions.explanation: The second sentence clarifies what the policy does instead of banning vehicles outright; “In other words” best restates the idea.

questions.text: The cave system is unusually extensive. _____, surveyors have mapped more than 180 kilometers of passages so far.
questions.explanation: The mapped distance provides strong evidence for the claim that the cave system is extensive, so “Indeed” fits.

questions.text: The northern population migrates hundreds of kilometers each winter. _____, the southern population travels long distances seasonally.
questions.explanation: Both populations migrate long distances seasonally, so “Similarly” is appropriate.

questions.text: The first prototype was expensive to manufacture. _____, its unusually low energy use made further development worthwhile.
questions.explanation: “Granted” introduces a concession: although the first prototype was expensive, its low energy use justified further development.

questions.text: The team could repair the damaged sensor array. _____, it could replace the entire unit with a newer model.
questions.explanation: The sentence presents two possible actions: repair the array or, alternatively, replace it.

questions.text: The study included only 42 participants, so its conclusions should be interpreted cautiously. _____, the results are consistent with those of several larger studies.
questions.explanation: “That said” acknowledges the limitation while introducing evidence that still supports the findings.

questions.text: The restoration project focused on one urgent problem: _____, saltwater intrusion into the freshwater marsh.
questions.explanation: “Namely” introduces the specific urgent problem: saltwater intrusion.

questions.text: A larger sample can reduce the influence of unusual individual cases. _____, a very small sample can make such cases disproportionately important.
questions.explanation: The second sentence applies the same sampling logic in the opposite case, so “By the same token” is appropriate.

questions.text: The reserve receives most of its rainfall in a brief three-month period. _____, managers store water during the wet season for use later in the year.
questions.explanation: Because rainfall is concentrated in a short wet season, managers plan storage with that fact in mind.

questions.text: The new method is faster, requires less material, and produces results as accurate as the older procedure. _____, it offers several practical advantages without sacrificing precision.
questions.explanation: The final sentence summarizes the listed advantages, so “In sum” is correct.

questions.text: Which expression is equivalent to x⁴ · x³?
questions.explanation: When multiplying like bases, add exponents: x^4 * x^3 = x^7.

questions.text: What is the value of √196?
Which expression is equivalent to √72?
questions.explanation: sqrt(72)=sqrt(36*2)=6sqrt(2).

questions.text: A population begins at 600 and increases by 15% each year. Which expression models the population after t years?
questions.explanation: A 15% yearly increase uses growth factor 1.15, giving 600(1.15)^t.

questions.text: A quantity decreases by 12% each period. What multiplicative factor represents one period of decay?
questions.explanation: A 12% decrease leaves 88% each period, so the multiplier is 0.88.

questions.text: Which expression is equivalent to (2x³)⁴?
If √(x + 5) = 9, what is the value of x?
questions.explanation: sqrt(x+5)=9 gives x+5=81, so x=76.

questions.text: The formula Q = kr² relates positive quantities Q, k, and r. Which expression gives r in terms of Q and k?
questions.explanation: From Q=kr^2, divide by k and take the positive square root: r=sqrt(Q/k).

questions.text: A quantity grows by 8% every 6 months. In a model of the form A(1.08)^n, what value of n represents 18 months?
questions.explanation: 18 months contains three 6-month periods, so n=3.

questions.text: For x ≥ 0, which expression is equivalent to x^(5/2)?
If 8^(x+1) = 4^(2x-1), what is the value of x?
A quantity is modeled by P(t)=1200(0.81)^(t/2), where t is measured in years. By what percent does the quantity decrease each year?
questions.explanation: The two-year factor is 0.81; the one-year factor is sqrt(0.81)=0.90, a 10% yearly decrease.

questions.text: A culture starts with 300 cells and grows by 20% every 3 hours. How many cells does the model predict after 12 hours?
questions.explanation: SPR: Four 3-hour periods occur in 12 hours. 300(1.20)^4 = 622.08.

questions.text: If y = √((x - 3)/5), which expression gives x in terms of y?
N = 640(1.25)^(2t). What is N when t = 2?
A student wants to introduce biologist Rachel Carson and her best-known book. Which choice most effectively uses the notes to accomplish this goal?
options: Rachel Carson was born in Pennsylvania in 1907.
Biologist Rachel Carson wrote Silent Spring, a 1962 book that examined the environmental effects of pesticides.
Silent Spring was published in 1962, many years after Carson was born.
Pesticides were widely used before Silent Spring was published.
questions.explanation: Choice B introduces Carson by profession, names Silent Spring, gives its date, and states the book’s focus.

questions.text: The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two bridges. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: The Golden Gate Bridge opened earlier than the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge.
Both bridges are suspension bridges that cross straits.
The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge is in Japan, whereas the Golden Gate Bridge is in the United States.
The Golden Gate Bridge opened in 1937.
questions.explanation: Choice B directly states the relevant similarity: both are suspension bridges crossing straits.

questions.text: The student wants to state the study’s main finding. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: The researchers studied 120 students for six weeks.
Students who slept at least eight hours performed better on the memory task than students who slept less.
The memory task was administered after six weeks.
Sleep is important for many aspects of health.
questions.explanation: Choice B reports the key comparison between students sleeping at least eight hours and those sleeping less.

questions.text: The student wants to emphasize a chronological sequence. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: The observatory was completed in 1894 and later received a new 100-inch telescope in 1923.
The observatory received a telescope in 1923 because it was built in 1894.
The observatory, which is on a mountain, has a telescope.
In 1923, the observatory was already several decades old.
questions.explanation: Choice A clearly orders the 1894 completion before the 1923 telescope installation.

questions.text: The student wants to explain why mangroves are valuable to coastal communities. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: Mangroves grow in tropical and subtropical coastal regions.
Mangrove roots can reduce wave energy and provide habitat for young fish, helping protect coasts and support fisheries.
Young fish often live among mangrove roots.
Some coastal plants tolerate salt water.
questions.explanation: Choice B combines coastal protection and fish nursery habitat to explain value to communities and fisheries.

questions.text: The student wants to contrast the energy sources while emphasizing one advantage of wind power. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: Wind and coal can both generate electricity, but coal has been used for longer.
Unlike coal, wind power produces electricity without direct carbon dioxide emissions during operation.
Wind turbines depend on moving air, while coal is a fossil fuel.
Coal plants can operate at night, and wind turbines can also operate at night when wind is available.
questions.explanation: Choice B contrasts wind with coal and highlights wind’s lack of direct CO2 emissions during operation.

questions.text: The student wants to make a claim about how the artist’s technique changed over time. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: The artist exhibited paintings in both 2010 and 2020.
The artist’s 2010 paintings used muted colors and thin layers, whereas the 2020 works featured bright colors and thick visible brushstrokes.
The artist used oil paint in both series.
Bright colors are often associated with modern art.
questions.explanation: Choice B directly contrasts the artist’s 2010 and 2020 techniques using the relevant notes.

questions.text: The student wants to support the claim that the city’s bike-share program expanded substantially. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: The program launched in 2016 with 40 stations and by 2024 had 210 stations.
The program uses bicycles that riders can borrow.
The city added some stations after the program began.
Bike-share programs exist in many cities.
questions.explanation: The change from 40 stations in 2016 to 210 in 2024 directly demonstrates substantial expansion.

questions.text: The student wants to introduce a disagreement between two researchers. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: Both researchers study the same archaeological site.
Nguyen argues that drought caused the settlement’s abandonment, whereas Patel argues that disruption of regional trade was the primary cause.
The settlement was abandoned centuries ago.
Drought and trade can both affect settlements.
questions.explanation: Choice B accurately contrasts Nguyen’s drought explanation with Patel’s trade-disruption explanation.

questions.text: The student wants to explain the purpose of the experiment, not its results. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: Researchers exposed seedlings to three light levels to test whether light intensity affects growth rate.
Seedlings under medium light grew 12% faster than seedlings under low light.
The experiment lasted four weeks and used 90 seedlings.
questions.explanation: Choice A focuses on the experimental purpose—testing whether light intensity affects growth—without reporting results.

questions.text: The student wants to qualify the broad claim that urban trees always reduce city temperatures. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: Urban trees provide shade in many cities.
Although trees can reduce local temperatures through shade and transpiration, the size of the effect varies with tree species, canopy density, and local climate.
Cities with trees are cooler than cities without trees.
Tree species differ in height and leaf shape.
questions.explanation: Choice B preserves the benefit while adding the conditions that make the cooling effect vary.

questions.text: The student wants to explain concisely why the 1919 eclipse expedition changed scientists’ views. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: The 1919 expedition traveled to observe a solar eclipse.

Measurements during the 1919 eclipse showed that starlight appeared to bend near the Sun, evidence consistent with Einstein’s prediction and influential in increasing acceptance of general relativity.
Einstein had published a theory before 1919.
Eclipses allow astronomers to observe stars near the Sun.
questions.explanation: Choice B connects the eclipse measurements to Einstein’s prediction and explains why they increased acceptance of relativity.

questions.text: The student wants to make a cautious generalization about the relationship described in the notes. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: Every city with more public parks has lower summer temperatures.
Across the twelve cities studied, greater park coverage was generally associated with lower average summer surface temperatures.
The city with the most parks had exactly 18% lower temperatures than every other city.
Public parks always cause lower temperatures regardless of local climate.
questions.explanation: Because the study is observational, “generally associated with” is appropriately cautious and supported by the notes.

questions.text: The student wants to begin a brief narrative about the discovery. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: The cave contains mineral formations and prehistoric paintings.
In 1994, three hikers followed a narrow passage beneath the valley and unexpectedly entered a chamber whose walls were covered with prehistoric paintings.
The cave was discovered in 1994 and later studied by archaeologists.
Prehistoric paintings can provide evidence about past cultures.
questions.explanation: Choice B gives a chronological, engaging opening centered on the hikers’ unexpected discovery.

questions.text: The student wants to provide an overview of the research project. Which choice most effectively uses the notes?
options: The project lasted three years and used 24 sensors.
Researchers used 24 sensors across urban and rural sites over three years to examine how nighttime temperature and humidity differ between the two environments.
Urban sensors recorded higher nighttime temperatures.
The researchers used equipment to collect environmental data.
questions.explanation: Choice B combines method, duration, sites, variables, and the project’s comparative purpose without overfocusing on one result.

questions.text: A broad explanation proposes that sleep duration influences cognitive performance. A researcher predicts that students who sleep fewer than six hours will score lower on a memory test than students who sleep eight hours. The prediction is best described as a
questions.explanation: A specific, testable prediction derived from a broader explanation is a hypothesis.

questions.text: Researchers assign plants to receive 4, 8, or 12 hours of light per day and then measure growth. What is the independent variable?
options: number of leaves at the end
questions.explanation: Researchers manipulate the hours of light per day, making it the independent variable.

questions.text: In the same study, researchers measure each plant’s increase in height after four weeks. What is the dependent variable?
questions.explanation: Plant height increase is the measured outcome, so it is the dependent variable.

questions.text: A dataset shows that as weekly study hours increase, average quiz scores also tend to increase. This pattern is best described as a
questions.explanation: Both variables tend to increase together, indicating a positive relationship.

questions.text: A graph shows that as distance from a city center increases, average traffic noise generally decreases. This pattern is best described as a
questions.explanation: Noise decreases as distance increases, indicating a negative relationship.

questions.text: A scatterplot of shoe size and vocabulary score shows points spread randomly with no upward or downward pattern. Which description best fits the relationship?
questions.explanation: Random scatter with no upward or downward pattern indicates no clear relationship.

questions.text: Read this research summary: “A team examined how sleep deprivation affects reaction time. Participants who slept four hours responded more slowly than participants who slept eight hours.” Which set contains the most useful keywords?
options: sleep deprivation, reaction time, responded more slowly
questions.explanation: The terms “sleep deprivation,” “reaction time,” and “responded more slowly” preserve the research variables and result.

questions.text: For decades, biologists assumed that the species was active only at night. However, new camera-trap data show frequent daytime activity during the dry season. Which statement best captures the passage’s big picture?
options: Camera traps are widely used by biologists.
The species is nocturnal in every season.
New evidence challenges the traditional view that the species is active only at night.
Dry seasons are longer than wet seasons.
questions.explanation: The key shift is that new camera data challenge the traditional “only at night” view.

questions.text: Many urban planners once treated street trees mainly as decorative features. Recent research, however, indicates that dense tree canopies can reduce surface temperatures and slow stormwater runoff. What is the main idea?
options: Street trees are difficult to maintain.
Research suggests that street trees can provide practical environmental benefits beyond decoration.
All cities should replace drainage systems with trees.
Decorative features are unnecessary in cities.
questions.explanation: The passage shifts from decoration to evidence of practical environmental benefits from street trees.

questions.text: A researcher predicts that increasing water temperature will shorten the time needed for a tablet to dissolve. In the experiment, water temperature is varied and dissolving time is measured. Which pairing correctly identifies the variables?
options: Independent: dissolving time; Dependent: water temperature
Independent: water temperature; Dependent: dissolving time
questions.explanation: Water temperature is manipulated; dissolving time is measured.

questions.text: A theory proposes that greater access to green space reduces stress by increasing opportunities for outdoor activity. Which statement is the most appropriate hypothesis derived from that theory?
options: Green space is important in many cities.
Residents living within 500 meters of a public park will report lower average stress scores than residents living more than 2 kilometers away.
Stress can be measured in several different ways.
Public parks contain trees, paths, and recreational areas.
questions.explanation: Choice B is specific, measurable, and directly derived from the theory about green space and stress.

questions.text: Researchers report a correlation of -0.78 between weekly exercise time and resting heart rate in a sample. Which interpretation best matches this result?
options: People who exercise more tend to have lower resting heart rates.
People who exercise more always have higher resting heart rates.
Exercise time and heart rate have no relationship.
The result proves that exercise is the only cause of resting heart rate.
questions.explanation: A correlation of -0.78 indicates a strong negative association: more exercise tends to accompany lower resting heart rate.

questions.text: A passage reports that “as ocean acidity increased, shell thickness in juvenile oysters declined, especially at the highest carbon-dioxide concentrations.” Which set of keywords best preserves the research story?
questions.explanation: “Ocean acidity,” “shell thickness,” and “declined” capture the variables and direction of the result.

questions.text: Scientists traditionally believed that a certain desert moss became metabolically active only after rainfall. New sensor measurements reveal that the moss can also become active when it absorbs moisture directly from fog. Which choice best states the big picture?
options: Fog is common in every desert ecosystem.
Rainfall is the only source of water available to desert mosses.
New evidence expands the accepted explanation of when the moss can become metabolically active.
Sensors measure moisture more accurately than rainfall gauges.
questions.explanation: The new sensor evidence expands the accepted explanation beyond rainfall to include moisture from fog.

questions.text: A study examines whether sleep duration predicts reaction speed. The report states that participants sleeping under six hours had slower average response times than those sleeping seven to nine hours. Which evidence most directly supports the study’s central claim?
options: The study included adults from several age groups.
Participants completed the task in a quiet laboratory.
Average response time was 410 ms in the under-six-hour group and 330 ms in the seven-to-nine-hour group.
Some participants reported drinking coffee before the study.
questions.explanation: The group means of 410 ms vs. 330 ms directly quantify the slower responses associated with shorter sleep.

questions.text: What are the x-intercepts of y=(x+2)(x-5)?
questions.explanation: Set each factor to zero: x+2=0 or x-5=0, giving -2 and 5.

questions.text: For y=2x²-3x+8, what is the y-intercept?
questions.explanation: At x=0, y=8, so the y-intercept is 8.

questions.text: What is the x-coordinate of the vertex of y=2x²-12x+5?
The function y=-3(x+1)²+12 has a

questions.text: If x²+px+12=0 has roots 3 and 4, what is the value of p?
questions.explanation: For roots 3 and 4, the sum is 7 = -p, so p=-7.

questions.text: For what value of k does x²-6x+k=0 have exactly one real solution?

questions.text: What is the axis of symmetry of y=-2x²+8x+1?
A parabola has x-intercepts at x=-2 and x=8. What is the x-coordinate of its vertex?
questions.explanation: The axis of symmetry is midway between -2 and 8: (-2+8)/2=3.

questions.text: If r and s are the roots of 3x²-10x+2=0, what is rs?
questions.explanation: For ax^2+bx+c=0, rs=c/a=2/3.
